introduction.definition: A gas scrubbing system removes acid or toxic gases (H₂S, HCl, SO₂, Cl₂, NH₃) from a vent stream by absorbing them into a circulating liquid — here dilute caustic — in a packed tower. pH-controlled dosing keeps the liquor strong; an ID fan draws the gas through and discharges it up a stack.
applications: Process vents, tank vents and odour control

pressure.title: Pollutant falls as gas rises through the packing
pressure.description: Acid gases (e.g. H₂S, HCl, SO₂, Cl₂) are absorbed into the liquor and neutralised by caustic (e.g. H₂S + 2 NaOH → Na₂S + 2 H₂O). Counter-current flow keeps the strongest liquor meeting the cleanest gas, so removal can exceed 99 %. Design uses liquid-to-gas ratio, packing height (NTU × HTU) and pH control; spent liquor is bled off and fresh caustic added.

video_tutorials.title: Gas Scrubbing System — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Gas Scrubbing System.
A gas scrubbing system removes acid or toxic gases (H₂S, HCl, SO₂, Cl₂, NH₃) from a vent stream by absorbing them into a circulating liquid — here dilute caustic — in a packed tower.
pH-controlled dosing keeps the liquor strong; an ID fan draws the gas through and discharges it up a stack.
Typical applications include process vents, tank vents and odour control; emergency chlorine / ammonia scrubbers.
The cutaway reveals the internal construction: Recirculation Pump, Recirculation Pump — Shaft & Coupling (turning), ID Fan Impeller.
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Gas Scrubbing System.
Check pH, ΔP and recirculation flow.
Clean packing / distributor.
Replace packing / pump parts.
Watch for breakthrough: odour / emission. Common cause: low ph, low liquor flow.
Watch for packing fouling: ΔP rise. Common cause: salts / solids.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
